Hi Sophie —

Thanks for the questionnaire excerpt. Below are concise answers we recommend you include in the packet; I’ve attached our internal policy summary and a retention matrix that breaks timelines down by data class. If you need a polished PDF with redlineable language for procurement, we can produce that next week.

1) Region processing controls
- Hosted API requests may be routed to a customer-preferred region per tenant configuration (US, EU). For Geostore we can pin production tenants to the US region (us-west-2 / us-east-1) to ensure processing remains in-region.
- Smart routing: we default to the nearest healthy region but will enforce region pinning for business/contractual requirements.
- Note: transient cache shards may replicate state briefly for performance but are subject to the retention rules below and are not used for backups or long-term storage.

2) Retention windows (default / configurable tiers)
- API request logs (metadata, headers): default 90 days; configurable down to 30 days with dedicated capacity plan.
- Full request/response payloads (if customer elects to persist): default 30 days; recommended for debugging only.
- Embeddings and derived artifacts stored by the platform: default 365 days; option to reduce to 0 days (ephemeral) for Dedicated or Private deployments.
- KV/prefix caches: ephemeral by design; TTL aligned with session and typically < 24 hours unless explicitly configured.

3) Deletion / tenant erasure workflow
- Customer submits erasure request via Console API or support ticket.
- Control plane marks tenant data for deletion and initiates coordinated purge across: primary stores, cache shards, and active KV stores.
- Deletion is executed within the service and async confirmation is sent when background jobs complete. Typical completion: 24–72 hours for active stores; 7–30 days to account for de-duplication and in-flight backups depending on retention SLA.
- Backups: backups are retained for at most 30 days by default; deleted tenant data is not restored from backups beyond the backup retention window.

Attachments: Redwood_Data_Residency_Policy_v1.pdf, Retention_Matrix_Geostore.csv

If you want an explicit clause we can add: “Redwood will process Customer tenant traffic only in customer-designated regions and will execute tenant-level erasure within the timelines described above; Redwood will provide a signed deletion attestation upon completion.” Happy to discuss specifics.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Security & Privacy Operations
Redwood Inference

> Monica, can you paste the export procedure and confirm the 30-day snapshot TTL number?

Quick export and backup details to include:

- Audit log export: Admins can request a time-bounded export from the Console. Export produces a gzipped JSON lines file (audit_events_YYYYMMDD.gz) with retained metadata only by default. For customers requiring full payload export, we offer an option but it must be enabled and contractually scoped.
- Snapshot / backup retention: Standard hosted backups are retained for 30 days; for Dedicated we can extend to 90/180 days per contract. Private (on-prem) customers manage their own snapshot schedule.
- Deletion confirmation & attestation: After erasure jobs finish we generate a deletion report with job ids and row counts; we can consume that report into a signed attestation (PDF) upon request — standard delivery within 5 business days of request completion.

I'll attach a short doc with the step-by-step admin export instructions. Confirming snapshot TTL: 30 days (standard hosted).

Regards,
Monica Patel
